 Player Grades: Lakers vs. Hornets
 Grading every Lakers player’s performance from the team’s 118-114 win over the Hornets.
 by Jacob Rude Nov 18, 2026, 8:14 AM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 What a wild, weird night.
 Of course, Quentin Grimes will deservedly draw the headlines after that game. He was unbelievable in the fourth quarter and pulled LA from the brink of having its win streak snapped to an unbelievable win.
 But so many other things were so odd about the game. The Hornets, who came into the night as the worst 3-point shooting team in the league, shot 38.5% from three in the first three quarters. The Lakers, who have struggled to rebound all season long, had 16 offensive rebounds in the same span.
 Water eventually found its level as Charlotte shot 3-15 from three in the fourth quarter and overtime. The Lakers still grabbed four more offensive rebounds for a total of 20 on the night. Little about this game made sense, which made it one of most fun games of the season.
 So, let’s dive into the win . As always, grades are based on expectations for each player. A “B” grade represents the average performance for that player.
 Matisse Thybulle
 31 minutes, 7 points, 6 rebounds, 3 steals, 1 block, 3 fouls, 1 turnover, 2-6 FG, 2-6 3PT, 1-2 FT, +8 
 He’ll be remembered for his steal to seal the win late, which makes up for his turnover on an inbound earlier in the game. Let’s re-evaluate him as the inbounder.
 Grade: B 
 Jake LaRavia
 22 minutes, 4 points, 5 rebounds, 2 assists, 1 block, 1 foul, 1 turnover, 2-5 FG, 0-1 3PT, +11 
 The whole defensive unit that closed the game deserves credit because, even if the Hornets didn’t play Brandon Miller and Coby White due to minutes restrictions before Naz Reid was (presumably) concussed, they completely shot the water off for Charlotte.
 LaRavia was flying around the court to help do so.
 Grade: B 
 Kevon Looney
 17 minutes, 4 points, 8 rebounds, 2-3 FG, -7 
 These were…surprisingly manageable minutes from Looney? Are we grading on a curve from the beginning of the season when he was unplayable? Yes. Do the Lakers still need to get a backup center? Yes.
 Grade: B- 
 Quentin Grimes
 41 minutes, 47 points, 6 rebounds, 3 assists, 1 steal, 1 foul, 3 turnovers, 16-24 FG, 10-14 3PT, 5-6 FT, +5 
 There’s heat checks, then there’s HEAT checks, and Grimes was safely in the latter category. A couple of his shots felt a bit audacious but when you’re as sizzling as he was, keep firing away.
 We’ve seen many games of players catching fire in recent years, but few, if any, got as hot as Grimes was on Tuesday.
 Grade: A+ 
 Luka Dončić
 42 minutes, 36 points, six rebounds, seven assists, 1 steal, 1 block, 5 fouls, 5 turnovers, 13-34 FG, 5-16 3PT, 5-7 FT, +2 
 It feels wrong to give Luka anything more than a great grade for this performance in the long run. I mean, it’s 36-6-7 with some clutch buckets and playmaking late.
 But he didn’t start this game well, got into foul trouble from the jump and, generally, was off his game for a lot of the night. Just know that I thought about those things before giving him this grade.
 Grade: A- 
 Jarred Vanderbilt
 13 minutes, 4 points, 7 rebounds, 1 foul, 2-3 FG, -5 
 Vando just decided Tuesday was the night he was going to turn back the clock and become the offensive rebound machine he once was. Six offensive boards in 13 minutes. Seven of the team’s 19 second-chance points came with him on the floor.
 Grade: B+ 
 Ziaire Williams
 23 minutes, 1 rebound, 1 assist, 1 steal, 6 fouls, 0-1 FG, 0-1 3PT, +6 
 Simply, this was not a good game. Ziaire never got into a rhythm offensively and his aggressiveness was too much defensively.
 Grade: F 
 Sandro Mamukelashvili
 23 minutes, 3 points, 3 rebounds, 2 assists, 1 steal, 1 turnover, 1-8 FG, 0-4 3PT, 1-2 FT, -1 
 Right now, it’s feeling a bit too boom-or-bust for Mamu. His last six games have seen him score 7, 7, 23, 23, 4 and 3 points. There needs to be a middle ground there.
 Grade: D 
 Collin Sexton
 25 minutes, 10 points, 4 rebounds, 3 assists, 2 fouls, 2 turnovers, 3-12 FG, 1-7 3PT, 3-4 FT, +2 
 As much as I want to give Sexton credit for finding himself in the right spots to get open shots late, he missed every one of them. And that’s to say nothing of the other mistakes he made throughout the night on both ends.
 Grade: D 
 Carson Cooper
 18 minutes, 3 points, 4 rebounds, 2 assists, 1 foul, 0-1 FG, 3-6 FT, +6 
 Welcome to the NBA, Carson. The Lakers’ newest two-way signing still hasn’t practiced with the team but was thrown into the fire late in the game. His offensive rebound tap out to Grimes was an unbelievable play.
 Grade: B+ 
 Adou Thiero
 Only six minutes from Thiero tonight, who was pretty quiet in his minutes.
 JJ Redick
 Redick’s challenge was not a great one, but you are also kind of forced into a tough situation as Luka was adamant about wanting a review and it was his third foul. I don’t blame him for using it. I blame Luka for the foul…and the refs for some awful officiating.
 On the flip side, going to a zone seemed to throw off Charlotte and the defense down the stretch was stifling with the team loading up on the few playmakers the Hornets had left on the floor.
 Grade: A 
 Tuesday’s DNPs : Cameron Carr, Jaden Hardy, Bronny James
 Tuesday’s inactives : Arthur Kaluma, Walker Kessler, Chris Mañon, Austin Reaves
